messages.text: Jamaica level series with dominant win over England

metadata.summary: England failed to extend their lead in the Vitality Netball Horizon Series with Jamaica, as the visitors claimed a dominant 55-40 win at the Copper Box Arena.
metadata.content: England 40-55 Jamaica: Vitality Roses beaten in London as Sunshine Girls impress and level four-Test Horizon Series | Netball News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England 40-55 Jamaica: Vitality Roses beaten in London as Sunshine Girls impress and level four-Test Horizon Series Jamaica bounced back from losing their opening match to level the four-Test series against the Vitality Roses; England will travel to Jamaica to play further matches on December 5 and 6, as preparation continues for next year's Netball World Cup Sunday 22 November 2026 21:52, UK Image: Jamaica levelled the four-Test series with a 55-40 victory England failed to extend their lead in the Vitality Netball Horizon Series with Jamaica, as the visitors claimed a dominant 55-40 win at the Copper Box Arena. A day on from a dramatic 47-46 victory in the series opener at the same London venue, England were second-best as the Sunshine Girls claimed a comfortable victory and levelled the four-Test series. The visitors scored six consecutive points on their way to opening a 15-7 advantage after the first quarter, then the Commonwealth Games silver medallists extended their lead to 11 points by half-time. messages.text: Gary Neville on De Ligt selection and 'negligent' Man Utd

metadata.summary: Gary Neville accused Manchester United's hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen their back line as their 4-0 loss to Liverpool left them with the worst defensive record in Europe.
metadata.content: Liverpool 4-0 Man Utd: Gary Neville on Matthijs de Ligt selection and 'negligent' Red Devils | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Liverpool 4-0 Man Utd: Gary Neville on Matthijs de Ligt selection and 'negligent' Red Devils Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as head coach after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card; Red Devils have conceded 34 goals in all competitions this season - the most by any side in Europe's major leagues Gary Neville Football Expert & Columnist @GNev2 Sunday 22 November 2026 20:32, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville reacts to Manchester United's heavy defeat to rivals Liverpool and says it is tiring watching them sink to new lows Gary Neville accused Manchester United's hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen their back line as their 4-0 loss to Liverpool left them with the worst defensive record in Europe. Liverpool ran riot after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card at Anfield as goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz ensured Mauricio Pochettino suffered a horror start to his Manchester United tenure. United have now conceded 34 goals in all competitions this term. It is the highest total of any side across Europe's top-five leagues. The result keeps them second from bottom in the Premier League.
